Predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, constructed as the continuous signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest (positive=enlarged, negative=reduced, zero=unmanipulated); orientation: as_declared because larger values imply more siblings and hence more competition. Fitted model: OLS day_14_tarsus_length ~ net_rearing_manipulation + factor(hatch_year) + factor(chick_sex_molec) + rear_nest_CS. Uncertainty used 1,000 bootstrap resamples of rearing-nest clusters within year, preserving year composition; SE was the SD of bootstrap coefficients and df was 316 clusters minus 1. Complete-case analysis retained 2,538 individual chicks alive and measured at day 14 and excluded 1,182 of 3,720 records with missing model variables, predominantly unknown molecular sex. The negative coefficient means greater experimentally induced sibling competition is associated with shorter day-14 tarsi.

Predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, the realized number of competing nest-mates in the rearing nest after cross-fostering. Orientation: as_declared.
9d9cb685-40.why: This directly estimates the declared within-frame effect of sibling competition on nestling growth: more realized rearing nest-mates represent more competition, and day-14 mass is the growth outcome. The fitted model was OLS of day-14 mass on rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing with fixed effects for breeding year, molecular sex (unknown retained as a level), and rearing-nest hatch date. It used 3,315 chicks with non-missing mass, manipulation, and brood size from 397 rearing nests; uncertainty came from 1,000 whole-brood cluster-bootstrap resamples (seed 42). The negative coefficient indicates lower day-14 mass with greater competition.

dcb214c7-43.unit_estimated: Individual chick (2,367 chicks clustered in 292 rearing broods within year)
dcb214c7-43.why: The fitted analysis directly answers the declared estimand within frame. Complete-case analysis excluded 1,353 of 3,720 chicks for missing covariates, predominantly molecular sex. Thus the model estimates the effect of sibling competition on nestling growth on the requested native scale.

Using 3,594 complete-case chicks, it modeled day_14_weight as a function of rearing-brood treatment (rear_nest_trt 5=enlarged, 6=reduced reference, 7=unmanipulated), factor(hatch_year), and rear_nest_CS, with a random intercept for rearing nest within year. The focal native-scale estimate is -1.0723 g (SE 0.0936 g; t=-11.46, df=3588, p<0.001) for the indicator coded 1=enlarged/high sibling competition versus 0=reduced/low sibling competition. This predictor is oriented as_declared, so the negative estimate means greater sibling competition lowers day-14 mass.

f97580e7-45.unit_estimated: Chick-level size-corrected day-14 mass (grams) per one net chick added to the rearing brood
f97580e7-45.why: The fitted coefficient directly targets the declared within-frame effect of experimentally manipulated sibling competition on nestling growth. d16afbfd-49.unit_estimated: -0.1529 grams of day-14 mass per additional chick in the realized rearing brood (robust SE 0.0118 g; 95% CI approximately -0.1761 to -0.1297; t=-12.93, cluster df=399, p=3.5e-32).
d16afbfd-49.why: This directly targets sibling competition and nestling growth in the framed blue-tit dataset.
